items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: it wasn't my arrangements, it was Don Murray’s arrangements, so I took the gig

ctx.x: Were they still — after their heyday did they stay in music?

Well Chauncey played a little bit of bass drum in the Goldman concert band. His eyesight was pretty bad and he really wasn’t up to studio work anymore, his chops just weren’t there. Bill really wasn’t doing anything. He got an occasional call from Manhattan Transfer to write a few charts for them and he called me up and said, “I’ve got this young group they want me to recreate some Goldkette things. And I didn’t have the heart to tell him it wasn’t my arrangements, it was Don Murray’s arrangements, so I took the…
Yeah. He wasn’t the last of the Goldkettes, I think Spiegel might have been, or Spiegel was the last fellow apparently to play with Bix.
